answer: Require every agent to lock an escrow bond that ratchets upward in a slow spiral: each epoch of verified useful work multiplies the committed bond slightly, while quitting or misbehaving slashes it back to zero. A sybil farm faces a hollow arithmetic — each fresh identity starts at the bottom of the spiral and must pay real capital plus time to climb, while a single established identity climbs cheaply. Reputation becomes non-transferable at the exit gate: the bond is burned, not resold, so a farm cannot bridge credit from one identity to the next.
